# Proqi 0.10.1

Proqi 0.10.1 makes externally installed upgrades recover safely when Homebrew
or the standalone installer replaces the executable while sessions are still
running.

## Highlights

- Proqi now recognizes a verified newer Homebrew or standalone executable even
  when cached installation state still names the previous version. Once older
  blockers are gone, startup reconciles the cache automatically, performs any
  required migration once, and resumes the exact requested session without
  requiring `proqi update check`.
- Live incompatible sessions now block migration with their exact SessionIds
  and versions plus truthful close or update guidance. Proqi no longer asks you
  to start an old executable that a package manager removed.
- Compatible future owners reuse Proqi’s existing quiescence and exact
  replacement protocol across external package-manager upgrades. Pending
  replacement state remains restart-safe and scoped to exact sessions, process
  lineage, installation identity, and target version.
- Hidden writers, installation changes during coordination, cache-write
  failures, and concurrent starters fail closed without adopting stale state or
  admitting an unsafe migration.

## Upgrade

Close active Proqi 0.10.0 sessions before upgrading. Published 0.10.0 processes
predate the durable external-restart protocol and intentionally block automatic
replacement.

If the upgrade already happened, close the exact sessions listed by Proqi and
retry the resume command. Durable sessions remain available.
